idea-plugin.name: Split Window File Router
idea-plugin.description:
Keep headers and implementation files side by side without manually moving tabs.

Split Window File Router is designed for a two-column editor layout in CLion. When files open, it routes files with configured extensions to the right editor pane and all other files to the left.

  • Default right-pane extensions: h, hpp, hxx, hh, inc, inl, tpp, ipp.
  • Customize extensions in Settings > Tools > Split Window File Router.
  • Settings persist between IDE sessions.
  • With only one editor pane, files open normally.
  • Manually dragged tabs are exempt from routing, with per-project overrides that survive restarts and can be reset in Settings.

Create a side-by-side editor split before opening files. The plugin does not create splits automatically. Matching is extension-based, not based on include directives, paths, or filename glob patterns.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.2: Remove deprecated and experimental API usages.

1.1.1: Clear manual routing overrides when tabs are moved back to their default pane, and improve routing and focus behavior for newly opened files.

1.0.9: Clear manual routing overrides when a tab is dragged back to its default pane, restoring automatic routing for that file.

1.0.8: Focus newly opened files after they are moved to the other pane. Detect selection in the pane that actually holds the new tab, ignore the replacement tab CLion selects in the source pane, and stop switching panes before files open.

1.0.7: Add opt-in debug logging for routing and keyboard focus diagnostics.

1.0.6: Wait for newly routed text editors to finish loading before requesting keyboard focus. Cancel stale requests when selection changes.

1.0.5: Fix keyboard focus transfer to destination editor window when files are routed across splits.

1.0.4: Restore destination editor focus after routing selected files without requesting focus for background openings. Handle asynchronous tab drops without routing them back. Remember manual tab moves across restarts, with a per-project reset control. Route based on actual file location, including selection of already-open files.
